name: Date input
description: A typed date, entered in a native <input type="date"> or in separate day, month and year fields. Use it for dates people already know, such as a date of birth; use a Date picker when choosing from a calendar helps.
summary: Type a known date, such as a date of birth
htmlElement: <input type="date">, or a <fieldset> of text inputs

elements.name: Legend or label
elements.description: <legend> for separate fields, <label> for a single field

elements.name: Fields
elements.description: One date field, or day, month and year fields, each with its own label

elements.name: Hint text
elements.description: An example in the expected format, such as "For example, 27 3 2007"

elements.name: Error message
elements.description: Says which part is wrong, such as "Date of birth must include a year"

configOptions.options: Day month year, Month day year, Year month day

variants.caption: Month and year — two fields, such as a card expiry date

usageNotes: Use a Date input for dates people know without looking them up, such as a birth date or a card expiry date. Typing them is faster than paging back through a calendar.
With separate fields, wrap them in a <fieldset> whose <legend> asks the question, label each field (Day, Month, Year), and use inputmode="numeric" rather than type="number".
Show the expected format in a hint linked with aria-describedby, and size each field to its content so the widths suggest the format.
Add autocomplete values where they apply, such as bday-day, bday-month and bday-year, so browsers can fill them in (WCAG 1.3.5).
Native type="date" looks and behaves differently across browsers and follows the user's locale format. Test it with your audience before relying on it.
htmlOutline:
<label for="dob">Date of birth</label>
<input id="dob" type="date" name="dob">
